title: Reductivity of a smooth affine model descends along a ring colimit
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ a directed system of nonzero commutative rings, and $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ a nonzero ring [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a smooth affine group scheme $H_{i_0}$ of finite presentation over $\operatorname{Spec}A_{i_0}$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Group schemes and reductivity have the meanings of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]; in particular reductivity requires connected reductive geometric fibres, and no torus or pinning is part of this hypothesis. Write $H_i=H_{i_0}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_{i_0}}\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ for $i\geq i_0$, and $H=H_{i_0}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_{i_0}}\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. If $H$ is reductive over $A$, there is $i_1\geq i_0$ such that $H_i$ is reductive over all of $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ for every $i\geq i_1$. No injectivity, flatness or Noetherian hypothesis on the ring system is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.11, printed pp.88--89, implication from reductivity of the limit group to eventual reductivity of the models. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this group-scheme reductivity theorem.

proof.text: Work on the directed tail $i\geq i_0$, which has the same ring colimit: each original index has a common upper bound with $i_0$, so compatible cocones on this tail extend uniquely. Put $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with projections $p_{ji}:S_j\to S_i$ and $p_i:S\to S_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] the transition morphisms $p_{ji}$, being morphisms between affine schemes, are affine, and $S$ with the maps $p_i$ is the limit of the system $(S_i)$ in schemes; the affine-limit theorem gives the same identification, compatibly with these projections. Each $S_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Base change preserves smoothness, affineness and finite presentation, so all $H_i\to S_i$ and $H\to S$ retain these properties. The group operations base change by the fibre-product universal property, and their equations remain equations after base change.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.11, printed pp.88-89, proof; Conrad PDF WANTED locally, read online.

proof.text: Define $U_i\subseteq S_i$ to be the points where the identity component of the geometric fibre of $H_i$ is reductive, and define $U\subseteq S$ similarly for $H$. Applying the first clause of [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-fibre-openness] at each point of $U_i$ shows that $U_i$ is open. The field-extension invariance lemma, applied to the residue-field extension at a point of $S_j$ over $S_i$ (or of $S$ over $S_i$), gives $p_{ji}^{-1}(U_i)=U_j$ and $p_i^{-1}(U_i)=U$. Since $H$ is reductive, all its geometric fibres are connected and reductive, so $U=S$. Set $Z_i=S_i\setminus U_i$. These are closed, and $p_{ji}^{-1}(Z_i)=Z_j$, while $p_i^{-1}(Z_i)=\varnothing$.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.11, printed pp.88-89, proof; Conrad PDF WANTED locally, read online.

proof.text: Each underlying space $|S_i|$ is spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. Each $p_{ji}$ is spectral: apply the quasi-compact inverse-image assertion of [lem-a1-filtered-spectrum-topological-limit] to the two-term directed ring diagram $A_i\to A_j$, whose colimit is $A_j$. The constructible topology refines the Zariski topology, because quasi-compact opens form a basis in a spectral space and are open in its constructible topology. Hence the closed subset $Z_i$ is also closed in the constructible topology. If every $Z_i$ were nonempty, [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-constructible-closed-nonempty] would give a compatible family $z_i\in Z_i$. By the prime-family identification in [lem-a1-filtered-spectrum-topological-limit], this family comes from a point $z\in S$. But $p_{i_0}(z)\in Z_{i_0}$ contradicts $p_{i_0}^{-1}(Z_{i_0})=\varnothing$. Therefore $Z_a=\varnothing$ for some $a\geq i_0$. Pullback compatibility gives $Z_i=\varnothing$ for all $i\geq a$.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.11, printed pp.88-89, proof; Conrad PDF WANTED locally, read online.

proof.text: Connectedness requires a separate argument. For $H_{i_0}\to S_{i_0}$ let $Y_{i_0}$ be the locus where the geometric connected-component count is $1$. Its local constructibility follows from [lem-sfb-geometric-connected-fibre-locus-constructible], using finite presentation from step 1. Since $S_{i_0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, [lem-trf-locally-constructible-qcqs-global] makes $Y_{i_0}$ constructible. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-component-count-base-change], its inverse image in $S$ is all of $S$, since every geometric fibre of $H$ is connected. The same count identity identifies $p_{ii_0}^{-1}(Y_{i_0})$ with the one-component locus of $H_i$. A group fibre is nonempty because it has an identity point, so count $1$ is exactly connectedness here.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.11, printed pp.88-89, proof; Conrad PDF WANTED locally, read online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible] to $Y_{i_0}\subseteq S_{i_0}$ and the scheme limit of step 1. All stages are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, all transitions are affine, and $p_{i_0}(S)\subseteq Y_{i_0}$ by step 4. Thus there is $b\geq i_0$ for which $p_{ii_0}(S_i)\subseteq Y_{i_0}$ for every $i\geq b$. By step 4, all geometric fibres of these $H_i$ are connected.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.11, printed pp.88-89, proof; Conrad PDF WANTED locally, read online.

proof.text: Choose a common upper bound $i_1$ of $a$ and $b$. For every $i\geq i_1$, step 3 makes each geometric identity component reductive and step 5 makes each geometric fibre connected. Each whole geometric fibre over an algebraic closure of a residue field therefore equals its identity component and is reductive. For an arbitrary homomorphism $A_i\to\Omega$ to an algebraically closed field, with image point $s$, the fibre $(H_i)_\Omega$ is the base change of the fibre over $\kappa(s)$ to $\Omega$; it is connected because the geometric component count does not depend on the algebraically closed extension of $\kappa(s)$ [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-component-count-base-change], and its identity component is reductive by the clause on arbitrary algebraically closed extensions in [lem-sfb-geometric-neutral-reductivity-field-invariance]. Together with the smooth affine finite-presentation properties of step 1, this is exactly reductivity of $H_i$ in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. None of the arguments used injective or flat ring maps, or a Noetherian base.
